lines.speaker: Ari (Commander)
lines.text: Fifty years after the Apollo landings, we stand on the precipice of humanity's permanent frontier. Welcome to MISSION27.
lines.caption: Ari welcomes the crew to the 27-hour critical outpost evaluation.

lines.speaker: Maya (Systems Engineer)
lines.text: Shackleton Crater's rim offers near-continuous sunlight for our photovoltaics, but the thermal extremes and space weather won't give us a second chance.
lines.caption: Maya briefs on Shackleton rim environmental constraints.

lines.speaker: Nova (Life Support)
lines.text: Our closed-loop ECLSS and water recycling systems are tested, but before we fly out to the lunar outpost, we must certify every procedure on Earth.
lines.caption: Nova emphasizes Earth training certification.

lines.speaker: Leo (Science Specialist)
lines.text: From deep mantle basalt samples to monitoring our home planet via DSCOVR satellite feeds, the scientific yield will redefine planetary exploration.
lines.caption: Leo highlights the geological and Earth observation science goals.

lines.speaker: Ari (Commander)
lines.text: Touchdown confirmed at Shackleton Outpost. Habitat power bus is active and cabin pressure is holding at 101.3 kPa.
lines.caption: Commander Ari reports successful touchdown on the lunar surface.

lines.speaker: Maya (Systems Engineer)
lines.text: Solar arrays are deployed and tracking the low horizon sun. Rover telemetry is green. Ready for operations.
lines.caption: Maya confirms base power and vehicle systems.

lines.speaker: Nova (Life Support)
lines.text: CO2 scrubbers operating at 98% efficiency. Remember the golden rule: maintain at least 4.0 kW to life support at all times.
lines.caption: Nova sets life support priority.
